messages:
ashley: Heads-up — ticket #3456, customer reporting a flood of threshold alerts for `api.latency.p95` last night but the dashboard shows empty/zeroed buckets for the same periods. Alerts appear to fire on stale/compressed rollups. @lee @kevin can you take a quick look? Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/33X (customer masked)
lee: Can you paste the alert config + an example timeline where it fired? Also which retention/rollup policy the org is on?
ashley: Paste of alert config and one example timeline below.
```
{
  "metric": "api.latency.p95",
  "agg_window": "1m",
  "evaluation_window": "5m",
  "threshold": 500,
  "condition": "any",
  "rollup_policy": "compressed-v2"
}
```
Example: alert fired at 2028-03-17T12:05Z. Dashboard timeseries shows zeros for 12:00-12:05 (ingest gap). Ops log shows a rollup entry for bucket 12:00 with ingest_ts 12:04.
ops-bot: ALERT automated: `api.latency.p95` > 500ms triggered for acct redwood-cust-42 at 2028-03-17T12:05Z (rule id r-3321)
kevin: Looking at the rollup rows — stored `bucket_anchor` is `2028-03-17T12:00:00Z` but the `ingest_ts` is `2028-03-17T12:04:12Z`. Our alert evaluation aligns buckets using the console's bucket_align logic (align down to floor(window)), but compressed rollups sometimes get stored with a trimmed anchor (we previously normalized to seconds, not canonical anchor). For certain late-ingest cases that causes the console to pick the previous non-empty rollup as the evaluation point.
ashley: Repro steps I used:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://ingest.redwood.ai/replay?ticket=3456&start=2028-03-17T11:50Z&end=2028-03-17T12:10Z" 
2) query rollups: `GET /metrics/rollups?metric=api.latency.p95&start=2028-03-17T12:00:00Z&end=2028-03-17T12:06:00Z`
Curl output excerpt:
```
{"bucket_anchor":"2028-03-17T12:00:00Z","value":0,"ingest_ts":"2028-03-17T12:04:12Z","compressed":true}
{"bucket_anchor":"2028-03-17T12:01:00Z","value":0,"ingest_ts":"2028-03-17T12:04:15Z","compressed":true}
```
But alert engine used the 11:59 anchor for evaluation and found a stale non-zero value.
lee: I can repro locally with the ingest-replay tool — if rollups are compressed and later appended we end up with anchors that are inconsistent with console alignment math. Hypothesis: we do `floor(ts / window) * window` when computing bucket anchors on ingest, which for sub-minute or odd window sizes after compression causes off-by-N seconds. For windows <= 60s we should preserve original anchor or use round-to-nearest anchor if the rollup metadata contains `orig_anchor`.
jordan: Quick Q — is this only affecting Hosted or does Dedicated/private hit this too? Any billing or SLA impact to call out for the customer notice?
ashley: So far only Hosted customers (this ticket is hosted). CS reported ~6 duplicate P1 alerts overnight for that customer, plus they saw cost bump from alerting churn. We should include this in the incident notes.
kevin: I pushed a staging patch (patch id: 7891) that preserves `orig_anchor` in compressed rollups and uses it in the console alignment path. Rolling to canary now. Will monitor alert flapping for next 30m.
ops-bot: Deploy started: patch 7891 -> staging (kevin) at 1859012400
lee: After applying the patch in staging and re-running the replay, alerts no longer triggered on empty intervals. Suggestions:
- Backfill affected rollups to canonical anchors where possible
- Add a short-term mute for rule r-3321 for redwood-cust-42 until backfill completes
- Add a unit test for compressed rollup anchor preservation
ashley: I'll coordinate with CS to mute that rule and notify the customer. Also adding a note to the post-incident doc. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
